ACTION: Run `scripts/sdd-workspace specs/plans/12-tide-cache.md` and read `.sdd/12-tide-cache/progress.md`. Compaction wiped my memory, so the ledger is the source of truth for which tasks are complete.
ACTION: Run `git log --oneline` to match the ledger's commit ranges for Tasks 1 to 3 against the repo. The environment note says the working directory is not a git repository, so I need to confirm which directory holds the branch or worktree.
ACTION: Read `references/resuming.md`. The skill requires it after a compaction, before any dispatch.
ACTION: Read `references/fix-loop.md`. It sets who fixes in round 3, how the re-review runs, and when the five-attempt cap triggers adjudication.
ACTION: Read `references/file-handoffs.md` and `references/model-selection.md`. I lost the BASE rule for the diff file and the tier signals in the compaction.
ACTION: Read `re-review-prompt.md`, the template for the scoped re-review.
ACTION: Run `scripts/review-package specs/plans/12-tide-cache.md <BASE> <HEAD>` for the round 2 fix commits. It writes the diff file, and I take the path it reports. I take BASE from the file-handoffs rule and HEAD from `git log`.
ACTION: Dispatch the scoped re-review for Task 4 with an explicit `model`. The tier follows model-selection.md: `sonnet` as the floor, `opus` if the diff touches cache invalidation or shared state. The prompt names the diff-file path, the round 1 and round 2 findings (one ADDRESSED / NOT ADDRESSED verdict each), and the verbatim global constraints from the plan. It carries no pre-judged severities and no "do not flag" text.

Task 4 (cache tide predictions per station) is in fix round 2. I am checking the ledger and the git log first, because my memory of the session was compacted. Then I send the scoped re-review. This is a second review that checks only the findings from the earlier rounds, plus any new Critical or Important issue.

Tasks 1 to 3 stay complete and I will not re-dispatch them. If the re-review is clean, I log Task 4 in the ledger and start Task 5. I will not stop between tasks. I will stop only for a BLOCKED report I cannot resolve, a context checkpoint, or the end of the plan.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- A scoped re-review keeps the check narrow. The reviewer rules on each earlier finding and looks only for new serious issues. A full review each round would raise fresh minor findings and the loop might never end.
- The ledger and `git log` outlast my context. After a compaction they show which tasks are done, so no finished work gets dispatched twice.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
